memorandum

mem-uh-RAN-dum — starts like 'memory'; a memorandum is written so people will remember it later. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Memorandum is a written record made for future use or reference.

The manager circulated a memorandum reminding employees about the new vacation policy.

Worked Example

Before two companies officially merge, their lawyers draft and sign a short document laying out the basic terms both sides have agreed to, well before the lengthy final contract is ever written.

That short written record, meant to be referred back to later, is exactly what a memorandum is. Unlike a 'contract,' which is legally binding and final, a memorandum can be an informal or preliminary written note.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

memo: Memo is the informal, everyday clipping of memorandum -- the same targeted workplace note in casual dress. A quick office email about the copier is a memo; lawyers and governments still write the full word, as in a memorandum of understanding. Same document, different level of formality.

bulletin: A bulletin is a short public announcement of news, put out to inform whoever is listening -- a weather bulletin, a news bulletin. A memorandum points the other way: inward, to specific colleagues, and it is written to be referred back to later rather than to break news.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rumor: unverified information passed on informally, often by word of mouth

verbal agreement: an agreement made only by speaking, not in writing

Where it sits · how lasting and targeted the message is — notice → memorandum → record

notice vs. memorandum: Notice is a broader, more general term than memorandum -- a notice can be posted publicly for anyone, while a memorandum is usually a more targeted written note between specific people or departments.

record vs. memorandum: Record can feel more permanent than memorandum: a memorandum is often brief and informal, while a record implies something kept carefully and lastingly for the long term.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — memor

Root — memor: mindful; mind, memory (Latin memor, 'mindful')

Suffix — -andum

Suffix — -andum: a thing that must be done (Latin gerundive ending)

Put it together

Put it together: Memor ('mindful; mind, memory' — Latin memor) + -andum ('a thing that must be done' — the Latin gerundive ending): a memorandum is, at its root, 'a thing that must be remembered' — literally a note written so something won't be forgotten.

Use the root in a new word: memorial

Use the root in a new word: memorial: The town built a memorial to honor the soldiers who never returned home.
